thread.title: Ohio lawmakers introduce bill to expand E15 fuel access on state turnpikes
thread.title_full: Ohio lawmakers introduce bill to expand E15 fuel access on state turnpikes

author: G. M. Nadeau
title: Ohio lawmakers introduce bill to expand E15 fuel access on state turnpikes
text:
State Representatives Josh Williams and Roy Klopfenstein announced on Mar. 18 new legislation that would require all Ohio Turnpike service facilities to offer E15 blended fuel. The proposal was introduced during a press conference and aims to increase the availability of biofuels across the state.
The legislation is intended to support energy security, rural economies, and lower fuel costs for Ohioans. Williams said, “At a time when America’s national security is inseparable from our energy security, biofuels represent a practical, homegrown solution. By investing in E15 and expanding biofuel access, we are strengthening rural economies, creating jobs, and reducing our reliance on foreign energy sources.” He added, “The Ohio Fuel Affordability Act is about more than fuel it is about supporting the people who power our state, lowering costs for Ohioans, and ensuring that our energy future is built right here at home.”
Klopfenstein highlighted the agricultural impact of the measure. “As a farmer, I understand the importance of E-15,” he said. “Ohio is home to seven ethanol plants that together purchase 233 million bushels of corn annually from over 5,300 family farms across the state. However, only about 200 of Ohio’s more than 5,000 gas stations offer E-15. This fuel is typically more than 25 cents cheaper per gallon than traditional gasoline and is compatible with 9 out of 10 vehicles on the road today.”
If enacted, the bill would require the Ohio Turnpike and Infrastructure Commission to contract with authorized retailers so that E15 becomes available at all service plazas. Installation or retrofitting costs would be treated as turnpike projects funded through various sources such as revenues or grants. The commission would also need to report annually on progress and conduct a feasibility study within one year regarding biodiesel infrastructure expansion.
Williams serves District 44 as a Republican member of the Ohio House of Representatives according to the official website. He has contributed to measures including overdose-response protocols in schools according to the official website and has sponsored legislation related to escaped convict alerts and sex-offender registry protections according to the official website. Williams operates as part of the legislative branch according to the official website.
The bill awaits assignment of a number and committee referral before moving forward in the legislative process.
